nodes.title: RECOVERY / ASSEMBLE LATER
widgets_values:
The two amber recovery nodes are MUTED by default.

If all segments finished but final assembly did not, mute the main green Assemble node, enable both recovery nodes, and queue. They validate every SHA-256 checkpoint pair and assemble without rerendering the completed clips.

For an interrupted generation, leave recovery muted and set Loop Start's start_clip to the first unfinished clip.

nodes.title: Jsonr eference
widgets_values:
H3 LOOP PLAN — QUICK FORMAT

Use the built-in H3 Chain Plan scene editor, or open its JSON panel and paste
valid JSON. Use double quotes, no comments, and no trailing commas.

{
  "prompt_prefix": "Global subject, wardrobe, style and continuity rules.",
  "defaults": {
    "duration_seconds": 15,
    "steps": 20
  },
  "shots": [
    {
      "id": "intro",
      "prompt": [
        "Use <Picture 1> for the subject's identity and physical features.",
        "Her wardrobe remains unchanged throughout the sequence.",
        "",
        "Begin with an opening tracking shot backstage.",
        "End while she is opening the corridor door."
      ],
      "seed": 123
    },
    {
      "id": "street",
      "prompt": [
        "Continue through the already-opening door without resetting her stride.",
        "Keep the incoming camera direction, lighting and subject pose.",
        "",
        "Move from the corridor into the street.",
        "End with the camera beginning a left orbit."
      ],
      "duration_seconds": 10,
      "steps": 24,
      "seed": 456
    },
    {
      "id": "outro",
      "prompt": [
        "Continue the unfinished left orbit from the previous scene.",
        "Resolve the performance and finish on a calm wide composition."
      ],
      "length": 124
    }
  ]
}

SCENE OVERRIDES
- prompt can be one string OR an array of readable lines. The node joins array
  entries with real line breaks. Use an empty string entry for a blank line.
- duration_seconds: requested generated duration; rounded UP to H3's 17k+5 grid.
- length or frames: exact raw frame count; must be 5, 22, 39, 56...3592.
- steps: sampler steps for this scene, 1–10000.
- seed: fixed uint64 seed. Omit it for a deterministic seed from base_seed.
- id: unique scene name used by checkpoints. Changing it can change an auto seed.
- prompt: required scene prompt. prompt_prefix is prepended automatically.

LENGTH AT 24 FPS, context=22, anchor=head
- 5 seconds  -> raw 124 frames; clip 1 delivers 124, later clips deliver 102.
- 10 seconds -> raw 243 frames; clip 1 delivers 243, later clips deliver 221.
- 15 seconds -> raw 362 frames; clip 1 delivers 362, later clips deliver 340.
Later clips lose the 22 repeated context frames after Trim. Use length for
frame-exact control. Every non-final shot must deliver at least context_length.

PRECEDENCE
shot value > JSON defaults > H3 Chain Plan node defaults.

RECOMMENDED PLAN SETTINGS
- width/height: multiples of 32; 960x544 is a good starting point.
- context_length: 22
- encode_mode: video
- anchor_mode: head
- crop: disabled
- audio_mode: source_track for music videos
- audio_context_length: 0 in source_track; 22 for generated-audio continuity
- segment_crf: 18–20

RUN / RESUME
- New run: unique run_name and Loop Start start_clip=1.
- Resume at scene N: keep the same settings and run_name; set start_clip=N.
- Changing a completed scene's prompt, seed, length, model settings, references,
  or source audio invalidates its checkpoint history.
- Change generation_fingerprint whenever model, VAE, LoRA, references, CFG,
  scheduler, or another generation dependency changes.

SOURCE-TRACK WIRING
Wire the same Load Audio output to Loop Start, Current Shot and Assemble.
The source song must cover the complete delivered video duration.

nodes.title: SCHEDULED REF2VA — COMPILES @TAGS PER SCENE
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the same female easycore/pop-punk performer defined jointly by @hero_face for facial identity and @hero_look for full-body appearance, wardrobe, body proportions, and distinctive features. Preserve the exact reference styling: shaggy bright yellow hair with vivid pink streaks, dark eyeliner, a small silver septum ring, a black spiked choker with a silver center ring, a cropped black graphic T-shirt, black ripped skinny jeans, a silver hip chain, and worn black high-top sneakers.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The opening of a single uninterrupted easycore music-video take follows <Subject 1> from a backstage room toward a door as the first vocal begins, using @song for the performed song and musical backing.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve her facial identity, hairstyle, body proportions, wardrobe, colors, accessories, and distinctive features from @hero_face and @hero_look while allowing natural performance poses and expressions.
@song: reference - its English lyric content, female vocal delivery, melody, phrasing, rhythm, beat, and easycore/pop-punk instrumentation guide the generated performance without directly copying the source signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a photorealistic high-energy easycore/pop-punk music video presented as one uninterrupted moving-camera take. There are no cuts; camera movement, performer momentum, lighting, and physical space flow continuously into the next generated segment.
[Shot 1] A medium-wide front tracking shot begins in a dim backstage dressing room while <Subject 1> walks toward camera with relaxed confidence, the camera gliding backward at her pace. During the opening instrumental her mouth remains naturally closed; she rolls one shoulder and lightly catches the hem of her cropped black T-shirt, steps around a road case, and keeps moving toward a brightly lit door at the far end of the room. Practical fluorescent fixtures and a warm mirror-light strip slide past behind her, catching the vivid yellow hair, pink streaks, silver choker hardware, septum ring, and hip chain while creating strong parallax without any cut.

As the first vocal enters, <Subject 1> (S1) looks directly into the lens and sings with the energetic, clean female delivery referenced from @song, <d>[English] Left the room with the lights still on.</d> On “left the room,” she reaches the doorway while still walking; the camera eases into a three-quarter side angle and lets the lit dressing room remain visible behind her for one final moment. She pushes the door open with her shoulder and crosses the threshold without slowing.

Near the end of the segment the next phrase begins while she enters a narrow concrete service corridor: <Subject 1> (S1) continues, <d>[English] Hit the door and the hallway's gone.</d> The phrase remains in progress as the camera arcs around her right side. Beyond her, the corridor geometry begins to stretch unnaturally toward another opening, preparing the physical transformation that continues in the next segment. Keep her walking motion, the camera arc, and the door movement visibly in progress at the boundary.

overall_soundscape:
Low backstage room tone, soft shoe impacts, T-shirt fabric and hip-chain movement, and a door latch are audible beneath the performance.

non_diegetic_music:
@song is referenced for the fast easycore/pop-punk backing heard by the audience, including distorted guitars, bass, punchy live drums, melodic hooks, and the dynamic changes present in this song segment.

nodes.title: HOW TO WORK WITH V2
widgets_values:
1. Open the Scene Prompt Editor and select a scene. It edits the connected Plan directly.

2. Click @ Reference. The tray shows only references active for that scene and their current native labels. Hover an image/video tag to preview it. Hover audio for controls; it never autoplays. Click a chip to insert its stable @tag.

3. Queue from scene 1, or set Loop Start's range/resume controls. The Scheduled Ref2VA node compiles stable tags to native H3 labels and inserts no prompt text.

4. Review Gate pauses after each saved scene. Approve to continue, edit+retry to replace only that scene prompt, reroll for a new seed, or approve+stop to keep a recoverable partial.

5. Final Assemble uses %date:yyyy-MM-dd%. Existing exports are never overwritten: later runs receive _001, _002, and so on. The amber recovery branch remains muted until you need assembly without rerendering.

nodes.title: V2 SCHEDULE DEMO — WHY THE @TAGS MATTER
widgets_values:
The purple chain is evaluated once per scene. Use stable @tags in prompts; never hard-code native Picture/Video/Audio numbers when a schedule can change. The scheduler inserts no prompt text: write and edit every reference definition in Scene Prompt Editor.

Scenes 1–7: @hero_face = <Picture 1>, @hero_look = <Picture 2>.
Scenes 8–14: @hero_face is inactive, so @hero_look becomes <Picture 1> automatically.
Scenes 4–6: @performance = <Video 1>, @performance_audio = <Audio 1>, and @song shifts to <Audio 2>. Outside those scenes, @song is <Audio 1>.

The static picture/video schedule fingerprint is connected to Plan for checkpoint safety. The per-scene @song entry is deliberately downstream of Current Scene, avoiding a graph cycle; source-track audio is already fingerprinted by Loop Start. Replace every media filename and model selection before queueing.

widgets_values:
{
  "prompt_prefix": "MUSIC VIDEO MASTER CONTEXT

Replace this with your song/theme rules.

REFERENCE HIERARCHY:
@character = definitive performer identity from the Character reference sheet (<Picture 1>).
@typo = definitive typography / graphic language from the Typo sheet (<Picture 2>).
@music = source song timing reference when audio_mode is source_track (<Audio 1>).

PERFORMANCE RULE:
Only lip-sync in clips that include an exact lyric line inside <d>[English] ...</d>.
All other clips keep lips closed.

TYPOGRAPHY RULE:
Use @typo styling sparingly on major lyric hits.
Visible text must match the sung lyric line. Never cover the mouth.

FULL SONG LYRIC MAP (sing ONLY the line assigned to the current clip):
Intro: instrumental only.
Verse / Chorus: paste your exact lyric lines here.",
  "shots": [
    {
      "id": "clip_01",
      "prompt": "subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the performer defined by <Picture 1>. Preserve exact face, hair, skin, body, and wardrobe.
<Picture 2> is the typography reference for on-world lyric graphics.
<Audio 1> is the current song segment for timing when using source_track mode.
